extension.summary: Four colours of particles, random rules, and the patterns that follow
extension.description:
A Kodi screensaver port of the openFrameworks Particle Life app. Four colours of particles attract and repel each other under a randomly generated matrix of pair forces, and out of those rules come cells, chains, membranes, orbiting clusters and drifting colonies. The rules are re-rolled on a timer (60 seconds by default) so the pattern never settles into one look, and an optional "evolve" slowly drifts the matrix instead.
Everything is configured in the add-on settings rather than an in-app panel: particles per colour, simulation steps per second, re-roll interval, rule evolution, viscosity and friction, force strength, interaction range, wall repulsion, hard bounds and particle size. The simulation is CPU-side with a uniform neighbour grid, so 4,000 particles cost about 1.3 ms a step on a desktop, and the particles are drawn as a single stream of point sprites with plain OpenGL 2 / OpenGL ES 2. The simulation runs in a 900-pixel-high space that widens with the screen, so the force radii keep the original's scale on any display.
extension.disclaimer: This is a native add-on: it is built per platform and Kodi version (this one: Kodi 21 Omega on macOS, Intel and Apple Silicon, and 64-bit Android). It needs OpenGL or OpenGL ES 2.0. Particle Life was created by Hunar Ahmad (https://github.com/hunar4321/life_code, MIT); this is an independent native port of the same idea with its own simulation, renderer and settings.
